answer_text: Plant cells contain a pigment called chlorophyll, which plays a central role in photosynthesis. Biology as a field covers an enormous range of scales, from single molecules up to entire ecosystems. Chlorophyll strongly absorbs light in the red and blue wavelengths, which it uses to power the conversion of light energy into chemical energy. Living organisms share a number of common features across otherwise very different species. However, it does not absorb green wavelengths of light — instead it reflects them back, and that reflected green light is what we perceive when we look at a leaf.
